name: Casco Historico (Plaza Mayor and Cathedral)
tagline: Historic heart around the grand cathedral
description: The walled old town centred on the Plaza Mayor and the late-Gothic cathedral is Segovia at its most atmospheric. Cobbled lanes, cafes, and monuments surround you, and the Alcazar sits a short walk west. It is beautiful but touristy and hilly.
bestFor: Nomads who want beauty, cafes, and landmarks on their doorstep

name: Plaza Azoguejo and the Aqueduct
tagline: Lively hub beneath the Roman arches
description: The area around Plaza Azoguejo, where the towering Roman aqueduct meets the town, is a busy meeting point linking the old town to newer districts. It buzzes with visitors, bars, and shops, and everything sits within an easy stroll.
bestFor: Those who like being at the centre of the action and transport links

name: Juderia (Jewish Quarter)
tagline: Quiet medieval lanes steeped in history
description: The historic Juderia, tucked within the walls near the cathedral and old synagogue sites, offers narrow, atmospheric streets and a calmer feel than the main squares. It is rich in heritage, with viewpoints over the valley and a peaceful, residential character.
bestFor: Writers and history lovers wanting calm within the walls

name: Nueva Segovia and San Lorenzo
tagline: Everyday districts beyond the old walls
description: Outside the historic core, areas like Nueva Segovia and the old riverside quarter of San Lorenzo offer more modern flats, local shops, and lower rents. They feel residential and practical, with an easy walk or bus ride back into the centre.
bestFor: Longer-stay nomads wanting value, space, and local everyday life
